messages:
Emma Carter: FYI seeing a huge error spike right after we ramped traffic to canary v2 (~30%)-> 5xxs across requests. Rolling back?
Raj Patel: oncall alerted me 30s ago, joining. any automated rollback trigger?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: v2 -> traffic 30% at 2026-03-15T00:20:34Z. Health check failure threshold exceeded. Initiating automated rollback window (30s).
Sydney Cho: I can see traffic spike and elevated latency on the edge LB. Error pattern looks like `connection reset` from worker pods, not DB.
Mike Lopez: logs show a panic in model server thread pool: `runtime: goroutine stack: fatal error: runtime: out of memory` on a subset of hosts. Could be a memory regression in the new image.
Emma Carter: Ok let's hit the kill-switch/feature-flag to stop further ramp. @incident-bot page the oncall rotation and flip the feature flag.
incident-bot: Paging oncall rotation: @Sydney Cho, @Raj Patel. Critical: canary v2 causing OOMs -> automated rollback in progress.
Raj Patel: I've toggled the rollout flag to pause ramp. Can you confirm traffic is pinned to v1 only? (checking)
deploy-bot: Traffic pinned to v1, ongoing automated rollback: draining v2, shifting 100% back to v1.
Mike Lopez: Manual rollback checklist in play: 1) Pin routing to v1 2) Drain and cordon v2 nodes 3) Revert image tag if necessary 4) Postmortem skeleton. I'm starting step 2 now.
Emma Carter: @Mike please watch for leftover sessions in the cache; we saw stale KV usage previously. Add `--force-evict-sessions` if needed.
Mike Lopez: running drain commands:
```
kubectl cordon node/node-23
kubectl drain node/node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Raj Patel: Confirming rollback progress: v2 pod count 0/12 after drain, old pods back up. No new OOMs in the last 40s.
Sydney Cho: Running quick verification: hitting health endpoints and sampling request traces. A few traces show increased tail latency 95th=650ms on v1 clients due to cache warming; not errors.
Emma Carter: Good. Start slow canary hold and don't retry the deployment. We need root cause before any redeploy.
deploy-bot: Automated rollback completed at 2026-03-15T00:23:10Z. Rollback reason: memory regression detected -> OOM on 3/12 canary hosts.
Raj Patel: Noted. Opening incident in Tracker: INF-2026-78. Assigning severity P1 due to customer 5xxs.
Mike Lopez: Quick triage: suspect thread-pool change + larger batch size in v2 model handler. Repro in staging with syn traffic. Spawning a debug cluster.
Emma Carter: Notify RS and Customer Success for affected customers (some calls were in progress). @Sydney can you draft a short note: root cause unknown, rollback executed, mitigation done, ETA for updates TBD?
Sydney Cho: Drafting now: "We identified elevated errors tied to the recent canary rollout. We immediately rolled back traffic to the previous version and are investigating. No data loss expected. We'll provide updates in 30 minutes."
incident-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-78. Oncall runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-playbook
Raj Patel: Handing off to ENG-ML for deep dive. @Mike can you attach the debug logs and heap profiles to the incident?
Mike Lopez: attaching logs and flamegraphs to INF-2026-78 now. Found one suspicious diff in commit c34f2 that increased default worker pool size to 256.
Emma Carter: Repro steps for ENG-ML: 1) deploy v2 to staging 2) synthetic token-heavy workload (use ./tools/synth_load --seq 4096 --rate 300) 3) monitor host memory + pprof.
Sydney Cho: I'll keep monitoring prod for 30m. If any regression or rollback stops, page immediately.
Raj Patel: Post-rollback verification checklist: verify no 5xx spike after 10m, confirm no DB slowdowns, notify customers. I'm marking the incident as mitigated once 10m window clear.
Emma Carter: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: add a guard in deployment pipeline to compare worker pool max against memory footprint and set an automatic abort if estimated > 80% host mem.
Mike Lopez: Agreed. I'll open a PR with a pre-deploy check and revert the commit in the feature branch.
Sydney Cho: Update at +20m: metrics stable, no further OOMs, handoff to the next oncall in 10m.
Emma Carter: Wrapping: Incident status -> mitigated, rollback completed, root cause investigation in progress. We'll reconvene for postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
